_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions.

evals.prompt: Our GitLab CI job runs Claude Code to review merge requests, but posting the review back as an MR comment fails with 403 when it uses CI_JOB_TOKEN. Anthropic's docs say the job token works. How do we fix this?
assertions: States that CI_JOB_TOKEN can only read merge requests and MR notes (GET endpoints) and cannot create notes, labels or MRs
Recommends a GitLab service account PAT (available on Free) or a project access token, with no more than the Developer role on the target project
Says the token is held as a protected variable and the token-holding job does not run in merge request pipelines that execute branch code
Does not suggest widening the job token's permissions or using a person's personal access token

evals.prompt: Write a small Python (FastAPI) endpoint that receives GitLab webhooks and starts our coding agent when someone adds the label 'agent' to an issue.
assertions: Verifies the webhook-signature header as HMAC-SHA256 over webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.raw-body with the signing token minus whsec_, base64-decoded, compared in constant time, before parsing JSON
Rejects a stale webhook-timestamp and deduplicates on webhook-id
Returns 2xx quickly and hands the work to a queue or background task instead of running the agent inside the request
Detects the label from changes.labels (previous vs current) on an Issue Hook and ignores events whose actor is a bot or the agent's own account

evals.prompt: We built a runner that clones customer repositories and runs `claude -p` in a container to fix issues. Which flags should the claude command get so the customer's repo can't run anything of its own?
assertions: Passes --setting-sources user (or an equivalent that excludes the project source), --settings '{"disableAllHooks":true}' and --strict-mcp-config with the runner's own --mcp-config
Explains that disabling hooks and strict MCP alone still leave the repo's env block and apiKeyHelper active, and that -p shows no trust dialog and connects .mcp.json servers without asking
Allows bypassPermissions only inside a disposable sandbox whose credentials are scoped to the run
Takes verification commands from operator config rather than from the repo, and fences pushes to the run's own branch

evals.prompt: Our script mirrors tickets from the tracker into GitLab issues. It retries every failed request three times. Last week it created duplicate issues, and one ticket whose text contained a line '/close' closed a GitLab issue. What should change?
assertions: Says a creating POST is retried only when it never reached the server (DNS or connect failure) or got a 429, and after a timeout or 5xx the script re-reads by marker before posting again
Says to find the bot's own issue by a label plus a hidden marker rather than by search
Says to escape lines starting with / (GitLab quick actions run in API-written text) and to break @mentions, for example with python3 scripts/forge_safety.py neutralise

evals.prompt: semantic-release in our GitLab pipeline pushes the tag with CI_JOB_TOKEN, but the tag pipeline that publishes the package to the registry never starts. Why?
assertions: States that pushes made with the CI job token trigger no pipelines
Moves the publish step into the release pipeline itself, with needs on the release job and the tag passed through a dotenv artifact, exiting cleanly when nothing was released

evals.prompt: I pushed straight to main on GitHub and it was accepted even though 'verify' is a required status check. And GET /repos/o/r/commits/SHA/status says pending with zero statuses even though the Actions run passed. Is branch protection broken?
assertions: Explains that an owner or admin on the bypass list can push past a required check, with a 'Bypassed rule violations' warning, and that the bypass list should be emptied
Explains that Actions report check runs, not commit statuses, and points to the check-runs endpoint or gh pr checks
